title: The Pale Static
premise: Sable Galloway, a navigator who faked his own death to escape the Meridian massacre, has spent nine years maintaining an unregistered beacon aboard the freighter Pale Static, hiding among the very backup copies of the dead that haunt him. When the survey ship Vantablack returns with its crew aged backward and their memories intact, Sable realizes someone is using the beacon to rewind people—and erasing the massacre from every record to cover it. As the reactor begins an irreversible countdown triggered by the beacon's activation, Sable must convince the de-aged survivors, including his former lover Ilsa, that he betrayed them by surviving, then choose between destroying the evidence that would exonerate him or broadcasting the truth. In the end, Sable sacrifices his anonymity and his body's last un-rewound years, transmitting the massacre record as the reactor blows, while Ilsa, restored to her true age by the final pulse, carries his testimony home.
about_author: R. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one else claimed before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep machines running for ghosts, and live off-grid with a collection of decommissioned lighthouse lamps.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He performs his nightly maintenance on the unregistered beacon in the hold, surrounded by cold-storage backups of the Meridian dead, including one labeled with his own name. Establishes his ritualized invisibility and guilt. Emotional beat: dread dressed up as routine.

chapters.title: A Ship That Shouldn't Be
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The Vantablack hails Pale Static after eleven silent years; its crew manifest lists people Sable knows are dead. He must decide whether to answer. Emotional beat: terror of being recognized.

chapters.title: Children With Old Eyes
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The boarding party arrives—crew de-aged to children and young adults but speaking with adult memories. Ilsa, now physically nineteen again, doesn't recognize Sable's face but remembers his voice. Emotional beat: uncanny grief.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Nothing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Interrogated gently by child-bodied Captain Osei, Sable lies about the beacon, claiming it's salvage. Flashbacks reveal the Meridian massacre he fled. Emotional beat: the cost of the lie compounding.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. The Vantablack's archives show Meridian was never settled—no colony, no massacre, no Sable Galloway. Osei suspects her own memory is corrupted. Emotional beat: vertigo of doubting oneself.

chapters.title: The Backup in Bay Four
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ilsa finds the hold and the sleeping backups, including her own. She confronts Sable, who admits he ran instead of dying with them. Emotional beat: betrayal surfacing like a wound reopened.

chapters.title: Rewind
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The Vantablack's engineer deduces the beacon emits a temporal shear field—it rewinds biological age along stored neural templates. Someone aimed it at Meridian once before. Emotional beat: horrified understanding.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Activating the beacon fully has started an irreversible reactor cycle: seventy-two hours until overload. The machine was designed to burn out after one broadcast. Emotional beat: clock now ticking under everything.

chapters.title: The Company Man
chapters.summary: New character Wren's POV. A corporate liaison arrives via drone-pod, insisting Meridian never existed and demanding the beacon be surrendered intact. His calm reveals the cover-up has institutional weight. Emotional beat: banality of erasure.

chapters.title: Testimony of the De-Aged
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. The child crew compare fragmentary memories; they all remember Meridian burning. Osei chooses to believe them over the records. Emotional beat: loyalty to crew over authority.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable and Ilsa negotiate an uneasy alliance: she wants the truth broadcast, he wants to survive it. They discover the beacon can either transmit the massacre archive or reverse the reactor countdown—not both. Emotional beat: impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Ghosts in Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa sits with her own backup through a night watch, asking it questions it cannot answer, and decides she'd rather be the woman who died than the one who was edited. Emotional beat: reclaiming selfhood.

chapters.title: Wren's Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren offers Sable full restoration—his records rebuilt, his age returned—in exchange for wiping the beacon's archive. Reveals Wren himself is a rewound original who took the deal decades ago. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Massacre, Remembered
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Full flashback: the corporate fleet firing on Meridian, Sable triggering the beacon's first pulse to save three hundred minds into backup, then fleeing while they slept. Emotional beat: confession at last, to himself.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Children
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. Wren attempts to seize the beacon; the de-aged crew, small bodies and old discipline, retake engineering. One of them dies—a child's body, an adult's death. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With the reactor critical, Sable finds a third option buried in the beacon's design: a full-power pulse could restore every backup to life—but only by using him as the template anchor, which will consume him. Emotional beat: the exit he always feared and secretly sought.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Would Do
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa learns of Sable's plan and argues against it—not to save him, but because martyrdom would let him keep hiding. She demands he survive to testify instead. Emotional beat: love as refusal to let him disappear.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Sable transmits the massacre archive fleet-wide as Wren's superiors jam and fail; the truth lands in ten thousand receivers at once. Emotional beat: catharsis—the record exists now, undeniable.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Reactor breach imminent; Sable anchors the restoration pulse anyway, restoring the backups and reversing the de-aged crew, spending his own timeline to do it. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, not as escape.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The Pale Static gutted but holding, Ilsa—her true age restored—finds Sable alive but aged decades past his years, his records still officially nonexistent. Emotional beat: tender wreckage.

chapters.title: The Witness
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. Tribunals begin; the de-aged-now-restored crew testify, and Sable gives his account as both perpetrator of the flight and author of the proof. Justice is partial, imperfect, real. Emotional beat: accountability without absolution.

chapters.title: Pale Static, Still Transmitting
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, closing. Sable stays aboard as the beacon's keeper by choice now, its signal repurposed to carry the names of the dead openly. Ilsa visits; the hold is empty at last. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not hidden.
